basis: Intellectual disability and strabismus define the syndrome; esotropia occurs in 22/24 patients. Hearing impairment and endocrine abnormalities are occasional.
Localized corneal lipid deposition defines the disease; systemic dyslipidemia is not intrinsic to arcus senilis.
Spastic paraplegia, cognitive impairment and neuropathy define it; scoliosis occurs in 10/15 and pes cavus in 9/17. Cataracts and urinary abnormalities are occasional.
Postinflammatory fibrosis directly damages lung tissue; prior inflammation alone does not establish an ongoing immune-mediated disease.
Cutaneous vascular tumor; anemia is annotated frequent (30-79%), supporting blood involvement. Thrombocytopenia and consumptive coagulopathy are occasional.
Cutis laxa with joint hypermobility (4/4); gastric/colonic diverticula (2/2) and high myopia (3/4). Bladder diverticula (3/4) omitted under cap; cohorts are small.
Neurodevelopmental language-processing disorder; language delay occurs in 26/26 and cerebral white-matter abnormalities in 22/31.
Oocyte meiotic arrest causes reproductive infertility without an established endocrine or other covered organ disorder.
Bile-duct dilatation and congenital hepatic fibrosis define it. Associated polycystic kidney disease and recurrent cholangitis are separate diagnoses.
Inherited autoinflammatory disease umbrella; fever and episodic inflammatory symptoms do not establish common lasting damage to another organ across subtypes.
Inherited cobalamin-processing disorder; developmental impairment and neurologic dysfunction commonly affect symptomatic patients (~30%+), with variation among subtypes.
Congenital skeletal myopathy with skeletal abnormalities defines it. Ptosis reflects muscle weakness; a single reported septal defect does not establish common cardiac disease.
Primary CNS melanoma arising in the spinal cord; melanocytic origin does not imply skin involvement.
Structural skeletal myopathy defined by nemaline rods and muscle weakness. Respiratory muscle weakness does not itself establish direct lung disease.
Congenital retinal signaling dysfunction causes stationary night blindness and reduced visual acuity; no independent neurologic involvement is established.
Vasopressin deficiency is a neuroendocrine hormone disorder; polyuria reflects hormone deficiency rather than intrinsic urinary tract damage.
Severe intellectual disability, spastic paraplegia and structural limb defects are defining manifestations.
Inherited sinus-node dysfunction directly impairs cardiac rhythm. Syncope and dizziness do not establish neurologic damage.
Broad hematolymphoid tissue disorder encompassing lymph nodes and spleen; infection, lymphoma or an immune-mediated mechanism is not established across the umbrella.
Carcinoma in situ originates in the hypopharynx; the pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis under these definitions.
Developmental disability defines it; joint abnormalities (>50%), visual impairment (~50%) and congenital heart defects (~25-50%) are common. Renal anomalies (~25-50%) omitted under cap.
Neoplasm originates in the glottic larynx, part of the airway.
Focal inflammation of choroid and retina is an infectious or immune-mediated ocular inflammatory disease.
Deficient adrenal cortical hormone production defines it. Autoimmunity is only one cause; hypotension and electrolyte changes do not establish other organ damage.
Severe glycerol metabolism disorder; altered consciousness may accompany acute crises. Persistent neurologic or muscle damage is not established across infantile cases.
